html:
Domingo Paes was a Portuguese trader who came from Goa about 1520 to the city of Vijayanagara, now the ruins of Hampi. It was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, and he saw its king, Krishnadevaraya, in person. His report is one of the fullest accounts of the city at its height. He calls it Bisnaga.

This king is of medium height, and of fair complexion and good figure, rather fat than thin; he has on his face signs of small-pox. He is the most feared and perfect king that could possibly be, cheerful of disposition and very merry; he is one that seeks to honour foreigners, and receives them kindly … He is a great ruler and a man of much justice, but subject to sudden fits of rage …
In this street live many merchants, and there you will find all sorts of rubies, and diamonds, and emeralds, and pearls, and seed-pearls, and cloths, and every other sort of thing there is on earth and that you may wish to buy.
The size of this city I do not write here, because it cannot all be seen from any one spot, but I climbed a hill whence I could see a great part of it; I could not see it all because it lies between several ranges of hills. What I saw from thence seemed to me as large as Rome, and very beautiful to the sight …

In 1565 the armies of the Deccan sultanates sacked the city, and it was never rebuilt.
